name: d3
_comment: D-letter write campaign (plan D3a/D3b, 2026-09-30).  One campaign so every
insert          plain INSERT of new keys (bf vs stock): the pre-D3 insert path
replace         INSERT OR REPLACE of new keys: D3b's blind path; bf_noblind is
update          existing-row UPDATE: D3a; bf_noupd = SQLITE_BF_NO_UPDATE_BUFFER
mixed           read=50,update=50: does buffered UPDATE cost the reads anything
each at bf_group_commit 1 (durable, the paper-faithful mode) and 32 (bounded
DEFERRED durability, plan D2 -- report it as such).  stock ignores the group
axis, so its two cells are two more repeats of the same thing.
Larger-than-memory (4M x 100 B rows, 32 MiB budget, drop_cache) because D3b's
claim is read I/O: an insert that no longer faults in its leaf.  Read
read_MiB/op beside ops/s, and blind_inserts vs blind_no_leaf: the bitmap only
knows leaves some descent has entered, so the blind share grows with warmup.
What each mechanism must show, or it has not earned its keep:
D3a  update commits: 1 record frame, 0 page frames (bf) vs 1 page frame (noupd)
D3b  replace: fewer read bytes/op than bf_noblind at equal correctness

experiments.name: replace
_why: The blind path needs the child to be a KNOWN leaf, and the bitmap only
knows leaves a descent has entered: with ~120k leaves and random keys
the blind share climbs with warmup (d3_smoke at 2 s: 1% at group 1).
Read blind_inserts / (blind_inserts + blind_no_leaf) beside every number.
